title: Event-Camera Guided Motion Deblurring for Fast-Moving Objects
description: Fuses asynchronous event-camera streams with conventional RGB frames to recover sharp images of fast-moving objects, using the microsecond-resolution event timeline to reconstruct the per-pixel blur trajectory instead of assuming a globally uniform blur kernel.
summary: Standard RGB cameras integrate light over the exposure window, so fast motion produces blur that single-frame deblurring networks struggle to invert because the true motion trajectory is unobserved. Event cameras, by contrast, report brightness changes asynchronously at microsecond resolution, effectively encoding the motion path that caused the blur. This idea proposes a fusion network that treats the event stream between two RGB frames as a dense supervisory signal for the deblurring process: events are voxelized into a spatiotemporal grid, aligned to the RGB frame, and used to condition a restoration decoder that predicts a spatially-varying deblur kernel per pixel. The model is trained on a mix of simulated blur (RGB + synthetic events via ESIM) and a small real-world event-RGB capture set, and evaluated on high-speed scenes (sports, drones, traffic) where global-kernel methods fail.
method: Voxelize the asynchronous event stream between consecutive RGB frames into a spatiotemporal grid aligned to the blurry frame's coordinate system.
Encode the blurry RGB frame and the event voxel grid with two parallel encoders, then fuse features via cross-attention so event timing informs per-pixel motion.
Predict a spatially-varying deblur kernel (or residual sharp image) from the fused features using a lightweight decoder.
Train on synthetic blur+events generated with ESIM plus a small real event-RGB capture set, using a perceptual + L1 reconstruction loss.
Evaluate on high-speed benchmarks (GoPro-style, plus real drone/traffic footage) against single-image and video deblurring baselines using PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS.

evaluation.novelty: Event-camera deblurring exists (EDI, E2VID), but conditioning a spatially-varying per-pixel kernel predictor on voxelized events via cross-attention, rather than solving a fixed physical model, is a less explored combination.
evaluation.feasibility: ESIM simulators and public event-RGB datasets (e.g., HQF, RGB-DAVIS) exist, and the architecture reuses standard restoration backbones, so a prototype is achievable on a single GPU.
evaluation.impact: Robust deblurring of fast motion would benefit drone vision, sports analytics, autonomous driving perception, and any low-light/high-speed capture where motion blur currently degrades downstream detection.
evaluation.rigour: Evaluation spans synthetic and real captures with standard restoration metrics and ablations isolating the event-conditioning contribution from the RGB backbone.
risks: Event-RGB spatial and temporal calibration errors could inject artifacts that outweigh the deblurring benefit.
Real-world labeled sharp ground truth for fast motion is scarce, limiting quantitative evaluation to mostly synthetic data.
The approach may offer little advantage in low-texture scenes where events are sparse.
